criteria.criterion: Reading the request built for an approved work item shows the item's title, rung, source and evidence, plus the content of each cited record inlined as text. The request contains no bare reference to a records/ path as the only description of the work.
criteria.evidence: I read `approve_request` in crates/athena-core/src/work_decisions.rs. It writes the title, id, key, time and role, and the rung. It renders the source and each piece of evidence through `render`: a job becomes its request text, reading and outcome; a path becomes the file's content (fenced, clipped at 6,000 characters) or a directory's listing; a commit becomes its message. The integration test checks that the request contains the source file's content and the cited job's request text, and has no `records/work-items/` path. The actual item khz6 is under records/ and is absent from the snapshot, so it was not checked.

criteria.criterion: A new appended record type (schema, canonical path, validation) holds a work-item decision: approved with a job id, or rejected with a non-empty reason. A work item that has a decision is no longer open, and the store loads these records.
criteria.evidence: crates/athena-data/src/records.rs adds `WorkDecision` and `WorkDecisionState` (Approved { job } or Rejected { reason }). It also adds the `athena.work-decision/1` schema, the canonical path `records/work-decisions/<YYYY-MM>/<id>.json`, and a `validate` check that rejects an empty reason. A round-trip test is included. store.rs loads these records into `work_decisions` and counts their ids as taken. `open_proposals` and `find_open` treat any item with a decision as closed.

criteria.criterion: athena-cli has new subcommands to approve and to reject a work item by id. They appear in the CLI help, and `athena status` or an equivalent output lists open work-item proposals with their ids so the user can find one.
criteria.evidence: main.rs adds ApproveWork and RejectWork. `cargo run -p athena-cli -- --help` lists approve-work and reject-work. status.rs adds `work_proposals`, plus `next` lines suggesting approve-work and reject-work. display.rs prints a 'steward' section with id, rung, title, source and evidence. The test status_lists_the_open_proposal_with_its_id_and_nothing_else passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`. New tests pass: approving a seeded proposal-kind work item queues a job whose request text contains the inlined content of its cited evidence. Rejecting records the reason. A second decision, an unknown id, and an empty reason are each refused.
criteria.evidence: The work_decisions integration tests passed (5 of 5): approving queues a proposed job whose request carries the cited content; rejecting records the reason; a second decision is refused in both directions; an unknown id, a blind-spot item and an empty reason are refused, with nothing committed. The core work_decisions unit tests passed (3 of 3), and so did the data test a_work_decision_has_a_path_a_schema_and_round_trips. Athena's full `cargo test --locked` run passed 605 tests.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.
criteria.evidence: Clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` printed no warnings or diffs. Athena's own run of both also passed.

criteria.criterion: docs and CHANGELOG.md describe the new commands and say the decision is recorded as an append-only record.
criteria.evidence: CHANGELOG has a new Added entry saying the decision is recorded as an append-only `athena.work-decision/1` record. README gets a new row in its command table. docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md gets a 'Deciding a proposal' bullet. Its claims match the code: the 6,000-character clip, the path layout, and the refusals.

findings.summary: An unrelated status line lost one column of alignment
findings.evidence: The literal "invalid     " (12 characters) was changed to "invalid    " (11 characters). Every other status label is padded to 12 (`{label:<11} `), so the 'invalid' line now sits one column off. The request did not ask for this.

findings.summary: A cited directory is shown only as a list of its file paths, not their contents
findings.evidence: When a reference points at a directory such as records/jobs, the request shows up to 60 file paths and none of their contents. The reader still cannot open those files. This is acceptable for broad directories, but such evidence carries less than a cited job or file does.

findings.summary: Approval is recorded as soon as the reading exists, even if the user declines to run the job
findings.evidence: `approve_work` commits the Approved decision right after `ask` returns, before the user accepts or declines the reading at the prompt. If they decline, the work item is still closed and linked to a job that stays proposed. This mirrors accept_proposal and is not tested.

summary: The change does what was asked. `athena approve-work <id>` builds the request from the work item itself: its title, id, key, rung and role, then the content of the source and of each piece of evidence. That means a cited job's request, reading and outcome, a cited file's text (clipped at 6,000 characters), a directory's file list, or a commit's message. The request then goes through the usual `ask` reading. `athena reject-work <id> --why` records the reason. Each decision is a new appended `athena.work-decision/1` record under `records/work-decisions/<month>/`, with validation and a round-trip test. The store loads these records, and an item with a decision is no longer open. `athena status` lists open steward proposals with their ids and suggests the two commands. I ran the 5 new CLI integration tests, the 3 new core unit tests and the new record test, and all passed. The tests cover the inlined cited content, the reason being recorded, and refusal of a second decision, an unknown id, a non-proposal item and an empty reason. Clippy and fmt were clean, and the new subcommands show in `athena --help`. README, CHANGELOG and docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md describe the commands and the append-only record. Every changed file is on the deliverables list. I found three minor issues. A cited directory is shown only as a list of its file paths, not their contents. One unrelated status line lost a space of alignment. A decision is recorded as soon as the reading exists, even if the user then declines to run the job. My runs were in the snapshot only. The real work item 20261015-003903-khz6 is under records/, which the snapshot does not have, so I could not check its actual request output.
